Given the high confidence in an IDH-wildtype prediction, co-deletion is biologically improbable. Evaluating the imaging features independently, the tumor phenotype is antithetical to that of a typical oligodendroglioma. The presence of multifocal disease, marked enhancement, and central necrosis are all strong indicators against a 1p/19q co-deleted tumor, which are typically solitary, less aggressively enhancing, and non-necrotic. The deep gray matter involvement is also less common in oligodendroglioma. The evidence strongly supports a non-codeleted status.
